title:
Stage 1 forge tier — increment 3 (the FINAL stage-1 feature increment): lemma library mechanics (REQ-9). Authoritative spec: .design/stage1-forge-tier.md REQ-9 + AC-13; sequencing in .design/stage1-forge-tier-kickoff-plan.md. Builds on all merged predecessors (foundation #20 .. 2f #47): the Item::Forge Lemma surface (2a), forge fill / proof discharge (2e), the cert + cache.rs + review.rs machinery. REQ-9 trails usage and is last in dependency order. Follow the ACToR read-write-verify-commit loop; commit per coherent sub-unit; self-verify before each commit; revert anything that fails. If low on time or budget, STOP at a sub-unit boundary and report what landed.

STANDING SELF-VERIFY RULES (these caused CI-red in prior increments — do NOT repeat):
- Run python3 tooling/doc-drift.py and RE-PIN the audited-sha of EVERY design doc whose governed source you touch; run req-registry.py --check; finish 0-drift. (After any merge of main, trust CI's DRIFT list over a local run — doc-drift's simplified git log can disagree across merge parent ordering; GH #48 tracks the gate fix.)
- EVERY new test that invokes lake / the Lean spine MUST open with the lake_present() skip-guard like the sibling live engine::tests — CI test-shards have NO spine, so an unguarded live test FAILS instead of skipping.

SCOPE: REQ-9 lemma library ONLY. This is the last feature increment before the G1 gate (REQ-10), which is a SEPARATE step the orchestrator runs — do NOT attempt G1 / the README headline flip here.

DELIVERABLES (per REQ-9 + the resolved Q-register):
1. Per-project lemma namespace (Q1): lemmas (the Item::Forge Lemma from 2a) live in a per-project namespace.
2. Certified-only citation resolution: a proof citing a lemma (e.g. simp [melems_cons]) FAILS if melems_cons lacks a certificate — cite-an-uncertified-lemma is refused with the lemma named (AC-13).
3. Dedup-on-burn by statement hash with citation rewrite (Q1): burning a statement-hash duplicate REWRITES the citation to the existing lemma instead of storing a copy (AC-13: two identical lemmas under different names → one stored, citation rewritten).
4. dec wf accessibility-proof cache (Q7): dec wf accessibility proofs cached by (relation, carrier) hash in the cache.rs conventions (CHECK_SCHEMA_VERSION invalidation), invalidated like other certificates; a dec wf re-check hits the cache, observable via the cache layer (AC-13).
5. Burned lemmas surface in forge review (review.rs) like any certified item.
6. Proof sharing (Q6): one proof for f block may discharge several ens#k with shared let-style local lemmas; NO cross-function sharing except via a lemma.

GAUNTLET before each commit: cargo test -p forge; clippy -p forge --all-targets -- -D warnings; fmt --check; for any Lean touch, lake build + axiom probe; doc-drift 0-drift (re-pin touched docs); req-registry --check clean; forge check over conformance still matches all v1 golden certs with oracle_subset byte-identical for v1 items. AC-13 specifically: citing an uncertified lemma fails with the lemma named; burning a statement-hash duplicate rewrites the citation (test with two identical lemmas under different names); a dec wf re-check hits the accessibility cache. No stubs/TODOs.

REGISTRY: register REQ-9 as REQ-S1-9 (shipped) with typed evidence; regenerate the status view; req-registry.py --check clean. No hand-written ## REQ status table.

SCOPE GUARDS: no cage / combinator-menu change; do NOT flip the README/docs headline (that is the G1 gate, R-GATE-1); never stage .crosslink/hook-config.json or .claude/settings.json; additive certs only for v1 items. NOTE: git push is blocked for you by policy — commit locally, end with a clear summary, and the orchestrator pushes + opens the PR. One branch; ONE increment (3).
